findings.title: Spread-route capability vs lease-pool capability coupling is prose-only, not an enforced/tested invariant
findings.location: Decision C ('How spread route ids relate to lease pools') and Capacity-map data model (STATIC_ROUTE_CAPACITY.reasoner)
findings.problem: Every default coder.primary worker leases against the 'reasoner' pool regardless of which round-robin route id it got (including a 'general'-classified overflow route). Correctness of admission then depends on the operator setting STATIC_ROUTE_CAPACITY.reasoner to the summed slots of all spread code backends. The design documents this only as prose operator-responsibility; nothing enforces or tests it. Mis-setting under-admits (not a deadlock, and OmniRoute still queues, so it fails safe).
findings.fix: Add the already-listed 'Spread + lease agreement' integration test as an assertion that fails if codeCapableRouteIds.length > 1 while STATIC_ROUTE_CAPACITY.reasoner equals a single backend's slots, and/or put an invariant doc-comment beside the STATIC_ROUTE_CAPACITY.reasoner constant stating it must equal the summed real slots of every route in collectCodeCapableRouteIds once spread is configured.

findings.title: Behavior for custom routes classified 'long-context'/'reader'/'vision' in code spread is unspecified
findings.problem: The helper includes 'reasoner' and 'general' and excludes others, but does not state what happens to a plausibly code-adjacent 'long-context' classification; it is silently excluded from the coder round-robin, which is defensible but undocumented.
findings.fix: State explicitly that only 'reasoner' and 'general' classifications are code-capable for the coder round-robin, and that 'long-context'/'reader'/'vision' are intentionally excluded (reachable only via an explicit per-worker route).

findings.title: SMALL_FLOOR = 4 rationale is thin given maxPerCapability already seeds the liveness invariant
findings.location: Decision D and Bounds-seeding formula summary
findings.problem: With maxPerCapability already in the max(...), SMALL_FLOOR only binds when every per-capability capacity < 4, i.e. it adds extra lease-wait headroom inside Menagerie. The one-line justification undersells why a floor above maxPerCapability is desired.
findings.fix: Add a clause: SMALL_FLOOR lets a few extra workers queue in the lease pool (waiting-for-inference) rather than on the dispatch semaphore, so capacity freeing mid-batch is picked up without a dispatch-permit round-trip; it never exceeds maxLive and never affects deadlock-freedom.
